text.tspan: # A Klein Bottle — the next meme
A companion to *A Theory of Everything, in a Bottle*. Where that file bottled a
proof inside a glass flask, this one uses the only bottle that has no inside to
bottle at all: the **Klein bottle**, the surface with no inside and no outside.
* It states and **proves** two genuine, kernel-checked facts that are the
algebraic fingerprints of the Klein bottle:
- `Klein.non_orientable` — orientation collapses on a non-orientable surface:
in the mod-2 world that measures its twist, `-x = x` for every `x`. Going
"the other way round" is going the same way. This is exactly the `ℤ/2`
torsion that lives in the Klein bottle's first homology
`H₁(K) ≅ ℤ ⊕ ℤ/2`, and it is why the surface is one-sided.
- `Klein.euler_characteristic_zero` — the Klein bottle has a CW structure with
one vertex, two edges and one face, so its Euler characteristic is
`1 - 2 + 1 = 0` (the same as the torus, as it must be for a closed surface
that is a circle-bundle over a circle).
* As a **side effect**, running the compiled program (`lake exe klein`) reads
*its own source* and emits one self-contained animated SVG,
glued-with-a-flip → one-sided bottle — while a tracer bead glides forever
along the single surface, passing from "outside" to "inside" without ever
crossing an edge, and the full source of this file scrolls, sealed, inside the
The theorem is about a surface with no inside; the artifact seals itself inside
/-! ## The theory: the algebraic fingerprints of the Klein bottle -/
/-- **Non-orientability.** The Klein bottle is non-orientable: there is no
consistent choice of "clockwise". The obstruction lives in the mod-2 group that
records the surface's twist, and there `-x = x` for every `x` — reversing an
orientation gives back the very same orientation. This is the `ℤ/2` torsion in
`H₁(K) ≅ ℤ ⊕ ℤ/2`, the reason the Klein bottle has no inside and no outside. -/
theorem non_orientable : ∀ x : ZMod 2, -x = x := by decide
/-- **Euler characteristic.** The standard CW structure on the Klein bottle has
one vertex, two edges and one face, so `χ(K) = 1 - 2 + 1 = 0`. -/
/-! ## The bottle: rendering the Klein bottle as an animated SVG
Everything below is ordinary, terminating `IO`/`String` code. It draws the
iconic immersed Klein bottle, animates the four beats of its construction,
glides a bead forever along the single one-sided surface, orbits a small cosmos
of stars, and scrolls the full source of this file — the process of its own
making — sealed inside the glass that has no inside. -/
/-- Escape the five XML-significant characters so arbitrary source text is safe
/-- A tiny deterministic linear-congruential generator, so the starfield is
/-- The four beats of the Klein-bottle construction, shown one at a time. -/
"Glue left ∼ right, keeping the arrows aligned: a cylinder.",
"Glue top ∼ bottom, but flip the arrows: a twist.",
"The seam has no seam — one side, no inside, no outside. ∎" ]
def starfield (n : Nat) : String := Id.run do
s!"<circle cx=\"{x}\" cy=\"{y}\" r=\"{r}\" fill=\"#cfe3ff\" opacity=\"0\">\
/-- The animated construction steps, revealed one per beat beside the bottle. -/
/-- Split the source into `<tspan>` lines for the sealed scrolling column. -/
def sourceTspans (src : String) : String := Id.run do
out := out ++ s!"<tspan x=\"330\" dy=\"11\">{xmlEscape l}</tspan>"
/-- CSS for the animation (kept as a plain string literal so `{ }` are literal). -/
.step { font-family:'DejaVu Sans Mono',monospace; font-size:16px; fill:#eaf2ff; opacity:0;
/-- The filled body of the immersed Klein bottle (the bulb / flask). -/
/-- The outer neck tube: rises from the bulb, loops over to the right, and turns
back to dive through the wall of the bulb. -/
/-- The part of the tube that runs *inside* the bulb (drawn behind the glass),
plunging down toward the funnel mouth. -/
/-- One continuous loop along the single surface, for the traveling bead. It
threads the neck, dives inside, sweeps the bulb and returns to the start —
proof, in motion, that there is only one side. -/
/-- Assemble the whole self-contained animated SVG. -/
"The bottle with no inside — proved non-orientable in Lean 4, and drawing itself</text>\n"
-- The tube that runs inside the bulb, drawn first so the glass covers it.
-- The sealed scrolling source: the whole process, bottled inside the bulb.
-- The funnel mouth inside the bulb.
-- The outer neck tube (glass), drawn over the bulb.
-- The opening where the neck pierces the wall (the famous self-intersection).
-- A twist-coloured ribbon flowing along the whole surface: orientation, undone.
-- The bead gliding forever along the single one-sided surface.
header ++ defs ++ background ++ insideTube ++ body ++ source ++ mouth ++
neck ++ hole ++ ribbon ++ bead ++ title ++ stepLines ++ foot ++ "</svg>\n"
/-- Read this file's own source so it can be sealed inside the bottle. -/
return "-- (source not located at runtime; the theorem still stands) --"
/-- The side effect: bottle the whole process into one animated SVG of the
IO.println "Wrote klein-bottle.svg — the bottle with no inside, bottling itself."

svg.text: A Klein Bottle — the next meme
The bottle with no inside — proved non-orientable in Lean 4, and drawing itself
Glue left ∼ right, keeping the arrows aligned: a cylinder.
Glue top ∼ bottom, but flip the arrows: a twist.
The seam has no seam — one side, no inside, no outside. ∎
